doc.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Playing piano by ear, including at a house of prostitution
summary: He taught himself piano and played for waiting guests at an apartment brothel in Chicago around age 19 or 20.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. I didn’t take any lessons, really. I just sat down there and started playing by ear and learning songs. Then later on in life, it became a part of livelihood, because I used to play piano on the weekends at – to tell the truth – the whorehouses. I was young, but I could go in there and sit down and play for the guests who would be sitting around waiting for their turn with the ladies. I played piano at these places.
What was the name of that place?
I don’t recall. It was an apartment. It wasn’t a public thing.
Oh, I don’t know. Let’s see. I had to be in my early twenties: 19, 20, something like that, or teenage. I don’t – I know it’s very young, but . . .
